title: Node.js Timer Subsystem Optimisation
description: Implemented four alternative data structures in C to replace the min-heap in Node.js's libuv timer subsystem, with a full benchmarking suite comparing CPU overhead, memory usage, and timer accuracy.
paragraphs: Built C-level patches modifying core libuv source files (heap-inl.h, timer.c, loop.c) to integrate a Doubly Linked List, AVL Tree, Timing Wheel, and Hierarchical Timing Wheel as alternative timer backends. Each implementation was tested against the original min-heap under realistic workloads to evaluate performance trade-offs.

Developed a comprehensive benchmarking framework that measures CPU cycles, memory allocation, and timer firing accuracy across thousands of concurrent timers. The project demonstrates low-level systems programming skills, including manual memory management, pointer manipulation, and integration with an existing open-source C codebase.

title: TradingAiForge
description: A collaborative desktop application that enables users to build personalised trading bots through an intuitive point-and-click interface, with TensorFlow-powered model training and optimised C++ execution.
paragraphs: Built using React and TypeScript for the frontend with Tauri v2 for a lightweight cross-platform desktop shell. The backend integrates Python's TensorFlow for machine learning model training and C++ for performance-critical bot execution, including MetaTrader 5 compatibility for live trading.

Users define entry and exit conditions through the UI, which are used to train a model that learns trading patterns. The trained bot is exported as optimised C++ code for fast execution in live environments. The app supports loading, editing, and iterating on previous bot configurations.

title: FizzyQuizzy
description: A real-time multiplayer trivia game with an authoritative server architecture, built with React, TypeScript, Node.js, Socket.IO, and Docker.
paragraphs: Developed a 2D real-time trivia game where players compete in live rounds with instant score updates. The frontend is built with React and Vite for a fast, responsive UI, while the backend uses a TypeScript Node.js server with Socket.IO for low-latency WebSocket communication.

The server uses an authoritative architecture to prevent cheating, validating all answers and game state server-side. The entire stack is containerised with Docker for consistent deployment on a VPS, supporting multiple concurrent game rooms.

title: VPS Server Hosting
description: Self-managed Linux VPS hosting my portfolio, game backends, and web applications with NGINX, hardened SSH, and firewall configuration, maintaining 99.9% uptime.
paragraphs: Configured a VPS from scratch with a secure Linux environment, including UFW firewall rules, SSH key-based authentication with password login disabled, and SSL certificate management. NGINX serves as a reverse proxy for multiple applications and static sites.

The server hosts my portfolio website, the multiplayer game backend, and several freelance projects. It has been optimised to handle 50+ concurrent users and has maintained 99.9% uptime since launch, giving me full control over deployment and performance.

title: 1v1 Scramble Game Backend
description: A real-time multiplayer game backend built in Rust with WebSockets, achieving 40% faster response times than the original Python prototype.
paragraphs: Originally prototyped in Python, I rebuilt the backend in Rust for its performance characteristics, reducing response times by 40%. The server handles matchmaking, game logic, and real-time synchronisation with the React frontend via WebSockets.

This project required adapting from OOP to Rust's ownership model. The result is a highly scalable backend with efficient word scrambling logic, support for up to 8 concurrent players, and deployment on a VPS with NGINX reverse proxying.

title: FDM Expense App
description: A full-stack expense management system built with React.js, Django, and MySQL, replacing manual Excel-based tracking and reducing processing time by 70%.
paragraphs: Led backend development in a 6-person Agile team, owning the API and database architecture. The system introduced automated form validation, manager approval workflows, and real-time claim tracking, eliminating errors and manual verification delays.

I played a key role in ensuring code consistency and best practices across the team. When faced with inconsistent coding standards, I facilitated discussions on structured development, leading to a more maintainable and scalable codebase.

title: Full-stack Portfolio
description: My personal portfolio website built with React 19, Vite, Material UI, Framer Motion, and Tailwind CSS, featuring dark mode, an admin CMS, a multiplayer mini-game, and a hidden trading dashboard.
paragraphs: This portfolio showcases my work with a modern UI featuring animated transitions, dark/light mode, and dynamic content managed through a built-in admin CMS panel. The site includes a hidden trading dashboard with live chart visualisation and a multiplayer word scramble mini-game powered by a Rust WebSocket backend.

Built with React 19 and Vite for fast builds, styled with Material UI and Tailwind CSS, and deployed to a self-hosted VPS via rsync. The site has attracted 50+ visitors and serves as a professional showcase of my technical range.

title: LSC Invoice Builder
description: An invoice generation tool originally built in JavaFX, then rebuilt as a React.js + FastAPI + MariaDB web app, reducing manual entry by 80% for 500+ customers.
paragraphs: Engineered a custom PDF generation solution to avoid costly third-party APIs, with auto-fill features that assume default values for common fields. The JavaFX version was later rebuilt as a full-stack web application with React.js, FastAPI, and MariaDB, hosted on a VPS for remote access.

The web rebuild introduced real-time database lookups, a modern interface, and significantly improved the billing workflow. The system serves over 500 recurring customers and has reduced manual data entry by 80%, making it a core operational tool for the business.

title: Horse Racing Simulator
description: A Java Swing-based betting simulation game with smooth pixel-by-pixel animation, an in-game currency system, and over 100 players.
paragraphs: Developed a manual frame update system to overcome Swing's limited animation support, creating smooth pixel-by-pixel race movement. Players place bets based on race conditions, with an in-game economy that incentivises continued play.
The game attracted over 100 players with strong retention, demonstrating effective game design and user engagement. Built entirely in Java Swing with custom rendering logic.
